setups.title: The night out.
setups.who: For anyone who wants to be at the party, not documenting it.
setups.dek: Reachable if the plan changes, a camera that doesn't post, and a room that's loud but not too loud.
setups.situation: You go out to be somewhere. Then you spend half the night on your phone looking at the place you're standing in. The phone isn't evil; it's just the most interesting thing in the room. Until you leave it in the bag.

pieces.why: Calls, texts, maps and a camera. Small enough for a clutch, boring enough to stay in it.
Take the photos. See them tomorrow. Nobody gets a story tonight.
The loudest room made survivable, and they look like jewellery, so you'll actually wear them.
Blocks tracking by design. The phone goes in; the signal stays out when you want it to.

setups.breaks: Rideshare and splitting the bill. Book the car before you go in, and let one friend run the payment app. Everyone has done it for someone before.
setups.change: Next time, leave the phone in the bag for the first hour and see who notices.

setups.title: Quitting the feed, together.
setups.who: For two adults who keep catching each other scrolling.
setups.dek: Nobody wants to quit alone and become the boring one. So you do it as a pair.
setups.situation: It's 10pm, you're both on the couch, and both of you are watching strangers cook. Quitting solo fails because the other phone is right there, glowing. Doing it together turns it into a house rule instead of a personal failing.

pieces.why: Encrypted calls and texts, a hotspot for the laptop, and typing so bad you'll call instead.
One magnet by the front door. Both phones tap out on the way in.
The links you'd have sent each other on Instagram live here now. No likes, no feed.
Something on in the kitchen that isn't trying to keep you.

setups.breaks: Two-factor codes, ride-hailing and the one friend who only uses WhatsApp. Keep one old smartphone in a drawer as the household utility device. It lives there, not in a pocket.
setups.change: Month two: add a Camp Snap and stop photographing dinner for anyone but yourselves.

setups.title: The writer who keeps opening tabs.
setups.who: For anyone whose draft is one browser tab from being abandoned.
setups.dek: The words were never the problem. The forty-one other things a laptop offers every eight seconds are.
setups.situation: You sit down to write, open the doc, and then open a tab to check one thing. Ninety minutes later the doc is still blank. The fix isn't discipline. It's a desk where the internet physically isn't.

pieces.why: A keyboard with nowhere to go. Drafts sync out; nothing syncs in.
For when you have to use the laptop anyway: everything blocked, every device, same schedule.
Research and edits on paper-feel glass, outside, in actual sunlight.
Plot by hand, search it later, wipe it, start again.

setups.breaks: Research. You'll need the internet eventually. Batch it: one hour a day, on the laptop, with Freedom deciding when it ends.
setups.change: If $729 stings, drop the Daylight and get a library card.

setups.title: The first phone.
setups.who: For a 12-year-old, and the two adults deciding for them.
setups.dek: Reachable after practice, no browser in the pocket, and a camera that doesn't come with an audience.
setups.situation: They need to reach you after practice. You don't want a browser in their pocket. Every other kid in the class has an iPhone, and you will hear about it daily. The trick is making the alternative feel like a choice they'd brag about, not a punishment they have to explain.

pieces.why: Calls, texts, no browser. In yellow, so it reads as a flex rather than a sentence.
They still take photos. Nobody sees them until you get home, including them.
Every phone in the house charges here overnight. Yours too, or none of this works.
For the parents. Research instead of vibes, for when the group chat starts citing articles.

setups.breaks: They'll be the only one outside the class group chat. Most families solve it with one shared tablet for messages at the kitchen table: visible, time-boxed, never in a bedroom.
setups.change: At 14, trade the Flip for a Clicks Communicator or a Light Phone III, and let them earn the upgrade.
